# Pauli clock transfer: a uniform gap and phase path, with the norm gate separated

29 October 2026. The positive result below is a constant-overhead, constant-
penalty-in-N, two-body **bounded-dimension qudit** construction of an endpoint
with a uniform gap and a uniformly gapped local path to the code with product
ancillas. It is not a proof of stability against arbitrary physical perturbations
of that endpoint. The stronger full-Hamiltonian small Yin--Lucas-norm identity
asked for is not acquired; Section8 gives a structural obstruction for the
natural symmetry-preserving clock/SW dressing. No finite-temperature statement
is made. No physical model is run.

## 1. Inputs, ordinary methods and exact output

Let {S_c:c in C} be positive commuting nonidentity Pauli checks on N qubits,
with no minus identity in their group. Each check has weight <=w, each data
qubit occurs in <=r checks, and all check supports have bounded spatial range.
The target is Hcode=sum_c(I-S_c)/2. No independence of the check list is
assumed. The accepted RX/RZ family has w,r<=7; its bounded-density spatial
embedding remains the named primary premise.

Choose a constant L>=max(3,w), for example L=8 for this family. There is ONE
L-level clock per supplied check and no freely fixed cat sector. Its vacuum
is uniquely |0>. Each simulator term acts on one data qubit and one clock,
or on a clock alone. The construction needs O(N) clocks, bounded degree,
bounded interaction range and strengths depending on w,r but not N.

The ordered-product ring mechanism is ordinary: see
[König0901.1333v2](https://arxiv.org/html/0901.1333v2), especially the clock
construction and the many-clock convergence qualification in Section4.3.
Exact two-body topological phase constructions are also prior, notably
[Ocko--Yoshida1107.2697](https://arxiv.org/html/1107.2697v1) for toric/quantum-
double models. What is proved here rather than imported is a generic Pauli
reduction to weak product-clock sectors and a uniform local sensitivity bound
that pays their syndrome-energy remainder. The elementary contraction below
is an explicit finite-body/qudit version of ordinary Kirkwood--Thomas theory;
[BDL0707.1894v1](https://arxiv.org/html/0707.1894v1) is its controlling prior.

source_excerpts.text:
An explicit Pauli-ring construction gives a two-body bounded-qudit endpoint
with the exact code logical multiplicity and gap at least3/4 uniformly in
system size. A local path retains the code coefficient while turning off
clock hopping, and stays uniformly gapped. This is a positive ground-phase
transfer with fixed overhead/penalty in N, not a whole-band simulation.

The stronger full-Hamiltonian small Yin--Lucas local-norm identity is not
acquired. For this construction every symmetry-preserving clock/SW dressing
has a trace obstruction: its required error has weighted norm at least
(1/2)exp(kappa*checkweight). The independent excited-sector terms cannot be
called small merely by increasing the clock penalty.

The decisive uniform acquisition is the marked-wrap KT bound in `PROOF.md`,
Sections3--5. It proves the auxiliary spectral gap separately from the
ground-vector fixed point and bounds the entire higher-order syndrome
coefficient incidence sum, with no N factor or derivative modulo S_c^2=1.

The actual compiler emits `CLOCK_HAMILTONIAN.json` from the EXISTING retained
1336-qubit/1428-check algebraic level2 input. It constructs11424 two-body
qubit--eight-level-clock hops and their exact transformed sign tables in
0.1532s. This input's literal geometry is not acquired; bounded range for the
all-level theorem uses the source's qualified large fixed subdivision and
embedding premise. The uniform9554-bit penalty is not physically economical.

Remaining gates: arbitrary physical-perturbation stability of the two-body
endpoint, a two-body-QUBIT implementation, numerical useful strength scales,
preparation and any perturbed finite-temperature memory claim. Ordinary
König/KT and Ocko--Yoshida phase mechanisms are explicitly credited.

# Strong ordinary comparison and surviving boundary

The full proof and actual construction are in `PROOF.md` and
`CLOCK_HAMILTONIAN.json`. This note is a scope comparison, not priority
clearance. No theorem is inferred merely from a paper's title or abstract.

* [Bravyi--DiVincenzo--Loss--Terhal0803.2686v1](https://arxiv.org/html/0803.2686v1),
  Theorem1, already obtains O(N)-qubit two-body simulators with strength
  independent of N at fixed precision. The guaranteed error there is an
  extensive ground-energy error. It does not directly supply the weighted
  local-norm ground-phase identity needed here.
* [Bravyi--DiVincenzo--Loss1105.0675v1](https://arxiv.org/html/1105.0675v1),
  Section4, supplies the ordinary local SW and linked-cluster toolbox.
  Finite-order locality does not remove the excited-ancilla conditioned
  terms or isolate the entire vacuum band at constant penalty.
* [König0901.1333v2](https://arxiv.org/html/0901.1333v2) supplies the ordered-
  product clock mechanism. Its several-clock extension explicitly leaves
  a size-independent convergence criterion open. The Pauli simplification
  used here is stronger than treating general noncommuting link operators:
  mixed words can only create scalar signs and whole-check products.
* [Ocko--Yoshida1107.2697v1](https://arxiv.org/html/1107.2697v1) already obtains
  exactly solvable, uniformly gapped two-body toric/quantum-double models
  locally connected to their targets. It also charges composite particle
  dimensions. Thus neither first two-body topological order nor first
  exact logical degeneracy nor first local phase transfer is claimed here.
* [Brell--Bartlett--Doherty1407.4829v2](https://arxiv.org/html/1407.4829v2),
  Theorems6--8 and SectionV, proves effective-parent phase results with
  isometric/quasi-injective PEPS and topological-order hypotheses. Its base
  model is two-body on code gadgets, not automatically on the individual
  virtual particles (SectionVI.1). We have not supplied those PEPS/LTQO
  hypotheses for the RX/RZ family, and do not use this theorem as a free
  family-admission or full-simulator stability premise.
* [Harley et al.2024](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11297168/)
  shows important scalability barriers for stronger analogue-simulation
  encodings. Our path transports the ground phase, not the whole extensive
